subject.title: gateway HTTP ingress skips browser Origin check under auth.mode none (cross-origin CSRF on state-changing routes)

question: Should gateway HTTP auth reject disallowed browser `Origin` headers under `gateway.auth.mode: "none"`, matching the WebSocket behavior while preserving origin-less headless clients?
rationale: This changes the core Gateway security boundary for an explicit no-auth private-ingress mode, so the security owner should confirm the intended compatibility posture before implementation.

options.title: Mirror WebSocket Origin Enforcement
options.body: Reject disallowed Origin-bearing HTTP requests in all auth modes and keep Origin-less clients working; this is the narrowest security fix.

options.title: Document None Mode As Fully Unguarded
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document that `auth.mode: "none"` has no browser-origin protection for HTTP APIs.

options.title: Require A Separate Design
options.body: Pause implementation for a broader CSRF/private-ingress design if maintainers do not want the HTTP path to match WebSocket semantics.

recommendation.title: Mirror WebSocket Origin Enforcement
recommendation.body: Reject disallowed Origin-bearing HTTP requests in all auth modes and keep Origin-less clients working; this is the narrowest security fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest implementation and test history is Vincent Koc's trusted-proxy HTTP origin guard in the same auth helper path.
